label: input token j late in the original phase (position >= 6)
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter j during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at a late position. Every input j at t = 6, 7 or 8 activates it (precision 1.0 on dev), and j at t = 5 sometimes gives a weak activation. Magnitude rises with position: about 0.45-0.5 of max at t = 6, about 0.75 at t = 7, about 0.95 at t = 8. Whether the j is a repeat or a first occurrence barely matters. It never fires on j earlier than t = 5, on any other token, on the <DEL> step, or anywhere in the copy phase (including when j is being output or fed back). The only misses are weak t = 5 activations, which hold about 0.5% of activation mass.

issues: I could not refute the label. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 0.937, F1 0.968 and mass recall 0.996, with 0 false positives, so the claim that every input j in the original phase at t >= 6 activates it holds.

All activations occur in the original phase, and none at t <= 4 or t >= 9. None occur on the <DEL> step or in the copy phase, and none on any token other than j. This matches the 'never fires' claims.

All 1101 misses are t = 5 j inputs with tiny activations (0.02 to 0.11 of max). They hold 0.4% of activation mass. Only about 10% of t = 5 j inputs fire, and I found no subset that picks them out: L == 6 gives precision 0.099, L > 6 gives 0.099, and a preceding j gives 0.12. Widening the predicate to t >= 5 drops F1 to 0.78. So this is weak noise, not a missed class.

The claim that magnitude rises with position is roughly supported by the dev profile. Mean activation mass per firing step goes up from t = 6 to t = 7 to t = 8, though the t = 7 to t = 8 increase is small.
